events.title: Congress Establishes the Library of Congress
events.description: President John Adams signed a bill that set aside $5,000 to buy books for the use of Congress. The new capital in Washington, D.C. got a small reference collection.
events.significance: The collection grew into the largest library in the world. It is now a national treasure holding hundreds of millions of items.

events.title: Arrests in Constantinople Mark the Start of the Armenian Genocide
events.description: Ottoman authorities rounded up Armenian political, religious and cultural leaders in the imperial capital. Most of them were later deported or killed.
events.significance: This date is commemorated each year as Armenian Genocide Remembrance Day. The mass atrocities that followed killed an estimated one million or more Armenians.

events.title: The Easter Rising Begins in Dublin
events.description: On Easter Monday, about 1,600 Irish nationalists seized key sites in Dublin and proclaimed an Irish Republic. British forces put the rebellion down within a week.
events.significance: The harsh British response, including the executions of the leaders, shifted public opinion. This helped fuel the push toward Irish independence.

events.title: Space Shuttle Discovery Launches the Hubble Space Telescope
events.description: Discovery lifted off from Cape Canaveral carrying the Hubble Space Telescope. The crew deployed it into orbit the following day.
events.significance: Hubble has transformed astronomy. It has helped pin down the age of the universe and has returned some of the most iconic images of deep space.
